title: I have to ...
subtitle: I have to / she has to / I had to
summary: Use have to and has to to say what is necessary, had to for the past, and don't have to for what is not necessary.

lesson.heading: I have to take it three times a day
lesson.text: A man is in bed. He is ill. On the table there is a big bottle of medicine with a label: 'Three times a day'. He says: 'This is my medicine. I **have to take** it three times a day.' I **have to** do something = it is necessary for me to do it.

examples.text: I'll be late for work tomorrow. I **have to go** to the dentist.
Jane starts work at 7 o'clock, so she **has to get** up at 6.
You **have to pass** a test before you can get a driving licence.

lesson.heading: The form
rows: to do, to work, to go
to do, to work, to go
lesson.note: With *he*, *she* and *it* we say **has to**, not ~~have to~~.

lesson.heading: The past: had to
lesson.text: For the past (yesterday, last week and so on) we say **had to**. It is the same for every subject.

examples.text: I was late for work yesterday. I **had to go** to the dentist.
We **had to walk** home last night. There were no buses.
We did an exam yesterday. We **had to answer** six questions out of ten.

lesson.heading: Questions and negatives
rows: do I / does she have to ... ?
I don't / she doesn't have to ...
lesson.note: In questions and negatives we always use **do**, **does** or **did** with **have to**.

lesson.heading: do you have to ... ? / I don't have to ...
lesson.text: I **don't have to** do something = it is not necessary for me to do it.

examples.text: What time **do you have to go** to the dentist tomorrow?
Why **did** they **have to leave** the party early?
I'm not working tomorrow, so I **don't have to get** up early.
Ian **doesn't have to work** very hard. He's got an easy job.
We **didn't have to wait** very long for the bus.

left.label: must = my opinion
left.text: Use must when you say what you think is necessary.
examples: It's a fantastic film. You **must** see it.
Jane isn't well, but she doesn't want to go to the doctor. I told her she **must** go.

right.label: have to = a fact
right.text: Use have to when it is not your personal opinion, but a fact.
examples: Jane won't be at work this afternoon. She **has to** go to the doctor.
You **have to** pass a test before you can get a driving licence.

lesson.text: Do not forget *to*: *I have to go*, not ~~I have go~~. And in questions use do/does/did: *Does she have to work?*, not ~~Has she to work?~~

exercises.prompt: At the end of the course all the students ___ a test.
exercises.explanation: all the students = they, so we say have to do.

exercises.prompt: Sarah is studying literature. She ___ a lot of books.
exercises.explanation: With she we say has to: She has to read a lot of books.

exercises.prompt: Is it necessary or not necessary?

items.text: I have to go to the dentist.
I don't have to get up early tomorrow.
Jane has to get up at 6.
Ian doesn't have to work very hard.
We didn't have to wait very long.
You have to pass a test to get a driving licence.

exercises.prompt: It's late. I ___ now. I'll see you tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: It is necessary now, so we use the present: I have to go.

exercises.prompt: In tennis you ___ the ball over the net.
exercises.explanation: you + have to + verb: you have to hit the ball.

exercises.prompt: I went to the supermarket after work yesterday. I ___ some food.
exercises.explanation: Yesterday is the past, so we use had to.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the right result.

pairs.right: so she has to get up at 6.
so I don't have to get up early.

pairs.left: The bus came in a few minutes,
pairs.right: so we didn't have to wait long.

pairs.left: Ian has got an easy job,
pairs.right: so he doesn't have to work hard.

pairs.left: There were no buses last night,
pairs.right: so we had to walk home.

exercises.prompt: Liz has to go somewhere. Ask her: 'Where ___ go?'
exercises.explanation: In questions we use does with he/she/it: Where does she have to go?

exercises.prompt: Why is Sue waiting? She ___ wait.
exercises.explanation: It is not necessary, so we say She doesn't have to wait.

exercises.prompt: George had to wait a long time. Ask him about it.
exercises.answer: How long did he have to wait?
exercises.explanation: For a past question we use did + have to: How long did he have to wait?

exercises.statement: Julia won't be at work this afternoon. She must go to the doctor.
exercises.explanation: Julia won't be at work this afternoon. She has to go to the doctor. This is a fact, not my personal opinion, so we use has to.

exercises.prompt: I didn't have any money with me last night, so I ___ some.
exercises.explanation: Last night is the past, so we use had to borrow.
